source.title: Behavioral tagging is a general mechanism of long-term memory formation
source.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS)

confidence_rationale: Direct behavioural demonstration of a two-factor write-eligibility mechanism: a weak experience sets a transient, input-specific 'learning tag' that yields only short-term memory UNLESS a separate novelty/salience event within a critical time window supplies the plasticity-related products that convert it to long-term memory. This is a strong biological analogue of MECH-368's separation of write-ELIGIBILITY (the tag) from write-CONSUMMATION (capture of consolidation resources), and grounds 'plasticity_eligibility' as a real gated state rather than an engineering label. Held at 0.7 because it concerns hippocampus-dependent episodic/behavioural LTM, not durable world-model/policy weight updates, and the gating variable is novelty/PRP availability rather than MECH-368's fuller f(PE, salience, residue, goal_relevance) conditioning set.
failure_signatures: Behavioral tagging gates the consolidation of episodic/behavioural memory traces; it is NOT shown to gate durable updates to a predictive world-model or action policy, the path MECH-368 flags as under-covered. The analogy to E1/E2/policy weight-writes is structural, not demonstrated.

The 'second factor' that licenses long-term write is NOVELTY-driven protein synthesis within a time window, a narrower and more passive trigger than MECH-368's active per-event gate conditioned on prediction_error, salience, residue_status, goal_relevance and plasticity_eligibility together. Tagging shows eligibility-then-capture exists; it does not show the rich multi-input arbitration MECH-368 posits.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Weak training that normally yields only short-term memory is converted to long-term memory if it coincides (within a critical time window) with a novel experience; this requires newly synthesized proteins induced by the novelty and reflects a 'behavioral tagging' process analogous to synaptic tag-and-capture -- a weak event sets a transient, protein-synthesis-independent, input-specific learning tag that must capture plasticity-related products to become durable.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-368's distinction between an event being write-ELIGIBLE (the tag is set) and actually consummating a durable write (capturing the consolidation resources), and the reality of a gated 'plasticity_eligibility' state in its conditioning function. Also grounds MECH-361's preferential-write logic: which traces survive to LTM is gated, not automatic, and salience/novelty is the gate.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The gated path is hippocampus-dependent episodic/behavioural LTM, NOT the online world-model/policy weight-update path that is MECH-368's actual under-covered target. The licensing factor is novelty-induced PRP availability, narrower than MECH-368's multi-input arbitration. Animal behaviour (rats); transfer to a synthetic durable-write gate is by analogy and structural parallel, not demonstrated equivalence.
mapping.source_context: Rats; three learning tasks (spatial object recognition, contextual fear conditioning, conditioned taste aversion); weak-training + novelty paradigm with protein-synthesis inhibitor controls.

confidence_components.notes: Strong, well-controlled PNAS behavioural study generalising synaptic tag-and-capture to behaviour across three tasks. Mapping fidelity moderate: the eligibility-then-capture STRUCTURE maps cleanly onto MECH-368's eligibility/consummation split, but the path (episodic vs model-update) and the conditioning set (novelty vs multi-input) both diverge. Direction 'supports' for the structural principle that durable write is a gated, two-factor process.
